title: SDK contract evolution and migration guide
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This page documents Redwood's recommended strategy for evolving SDK contracts (public client APIs, CLI flags, response shapes) while minimizing customer impact. It covers principles, a repeatable migration workflow, testing and automation, rollout controls, and standard communication artifacts (deprecation notice, PR template, migration checklist). The guidance applies to all officially supported language SDKs, the CLI, and code snippets published on docs.redwood.ai.

Goals:
- Keep breaking changes as rare and well-signaled as possible.
- Provide a low-effort migration path for customers and internal integrators.
- Ensure docs, CI, and telemetry reflect live compatibility guarantees.
- Make rollbacks safe and fast.

Scope and definitions:
- "Contract": public surface exported by an SDK or CLI (function signatures, default values, enums, JSON response fields).
- "Minor compatibility": additive changes (new optional params, new fields in responses).
- "Major compatibility": incompatible change requiring client updates (removed or renamed params, changed return shapes).
- "Compatibility window": time between first deprecation notice and removal. Standard window is 90 days unless otherwise approved.

Principles:
1) Semantic versioning by intent: minor patches for fixes, minor versions for additive changes, major versions for breaking changes.
2) Dual-path rollout: when possible, keep legacy behavior available via a flag or compatibility toggle for the compatibility window.
3) Docs-first: update docs/SDK samples and central snippet registry in the same PR as code changes.
4) CI and telemetry: every SDK release must run the compatibility test suite and publish compatibility metrics.
5) Customer empathy: issue deprecation notices that include impact, migration steps, and an automated compatibility checker where feasible.

Compatibility matrix (example):

| Change type | Allowed without major | Required signals | Default behavior during window | Removal policy |
|-------------|-----------------------|------------------|-------------------------------|----------------|
| Add optional param | Yes | None | Backwards compatible | N/A |
| Add response field | Yes | None | Backwards compatible | N/A |
| Rename param | No | Deprecation notice + migration guide | Legacy enabled via compat flag | Remove after 90 days |
| Remove field | No | Deprecation notice + migration guide + tests | Legacy compatibility mode | Remove after 90–180 days with migration automation |

Migration workflow (authoring team):
1. Design and ADR: Create an ADR if the change affects public behavior. Include rationale, affected SDKs, and migration complexity.
2. Feature branch: Implement change behind a runtime feature flag or compat toggle where feasible.
3. Update tests: Add compatibility tests to the central compatibility harness. See 'compatibility-testing' below.
4. Docs and snippets: Update the docs site snippet registry and docs-site PR. Include before/after code samples.
5. Release plan: Draft deprecation notice text, set compatibility window (default 90 days), and schedule staged rollout.
6. Telemetry and alerts: Add a metric that measures clients still using legacy behavior (counter tagged by SDK version).
7. Deprecation PR: Merge code + docs + telemetry. Publish SDK minor/major versions as appropriate.
8. Monitor: Watch compatibility metric for 2x expected daily traffic for at least 7 days. If adoption is slow, extend window or add migration assistance.

Compatibility-testing (automation):
- Central harness repo: repo: infra/compat-harness. This runs the canonical tests for every SDK against the runtime matrix (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Test types: contract tests (JSON shape assertions), sample-run tests (execute docs snippets), e2e smoke with short-lived keys.
- Failure policy: any contract-test failure blocks release; sample-run failures are triaged within 48 hours.

Sample contract test (pseudocode):
```
# compat-harness/test_contracts/test_response_fields.py
def test_chat_response_contains_metadata(client):
    resp = client.chat(prompt='hi')
    assert 'request_id' in resp.metadata  # added field must exist
```

Docs site and snippet workflow (docs owners):
- Single PR rule: code changes that affect public SDK surface must include the docs-site change in the same PR. The PR must reference the snippet id(s) updated in the snippet registry.
- Snippet registry entry (required fields): snippet_id, language, original_file, test_command, expected_output.
- Docs CI validates that snippets run against the integration endpoint with a test key in the compatibility harness.

Deprecation notice template (publish to status page and send to all active API keys in the last 90 days):
- Title: Deprecation: <feature> in <sdk> (version X)
- Summary: Short one-paragraph description of change and reason.
- Impact: Which endpoints, SDK versions, and sample snippets are affected.
- Migration steps: Bullet list of code-level changes with snippet links.
- Timeline: Notice date, removal date, last date for compatibility flag.
- Support: Contact info (link to support playbook) and migration assistance SLA.

Sample PR checklist for SDK maintainers (add to PR description):
- [ ] ADR created/linked if major change
- [ ] Unit + integration tests added
- [ ] Compatibility harness green (link CI run)
- [ ] Docs updated (snippet ids listed)
- [ ] Telemetry metric added and dashboard created
- [ ] Deprecation notice drafted (if applicable)

Migration checklist for customers (to include in deprecation email and docs page):
1. Identify usages of deprecated API/flag in your codebase (grep, compile, or run the provided compatibility scanner).
2. Run the compatibility scanner (see tool below) and review the generated migration plan.
3. Apply code changes in a feature branch following sample snippets.
4. Run SDK integration tests.
5. Deploy to staging and run smoke e2e.
6. Roll out to production behind a feature gate if needed.
7. Remove legacy toggle after compatibility window expires.

Compatibility scanner (tooling):
- Name: redwood-sdk-compat-checker (Python/NodeCLIs).
- Usage example:
```
# scan a repository for deprecated SDK patterns
redwood-sdk-compat-checker scan --path ./my-service --lang python --report report.json
```
- Output: JSON report with instances found, suggested changes, and confidence scores.

Rollback and emergency policy:
- If a change causes severe regressions (P1/P2), maintainers must be able to flip the compat toggle or push a patch within 60 minutes during business hours.
- SRE runbook: eng-sre/runbooks/compat-rollbacks. Steps include toggling flags, hotfix release commands, and customer comms template.

Monitoring & SLOs for migrations:
- Migration adoption SLO: 90% of active clients should be migrated from legacy behavior within the compatibility window.
- Observability KPIs: number of requests using legacy code path, error rate for migrated clients, mean time to migration per client.
- Dashboards: eng-platform/dashboard/sdk-migrations (owner: devx-team).

Communication and internal process:
- Notify the Developer Experience Slack channel (#devx-sdk-changes) at the start of the compatibility window and weekly during the window.
- For high-impact changes, schedule a Q&A office hour and publish a short explainer video.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: SDK maintainer (team and individual listed in the PR).
- Secondary owner: Runtime product manager (for behavioral changes).
- Escalation path: SDK maintainer -> Runtime PM -> Eng SRE -> Head of DevX.

Appendix A — Example migration: rename 'streaming' param to 'response_mode' (safe approach):
1) ADR filed: 2025-10-20 (link).
2) Implement 'response_mode' while keeping 'streaming' as alias. Both accepted by client with deprecation warning when 'streaming' provided.
3) Add compatibility tests that assert both flags work.
4) Release minor SDK bump with telemetry and deprecation notice.
5) After 90 days, remove alias and publish major bump.

Code snippet (before -> after):
Before (Python):
```
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=..., streaming=True)
```
After (Python):
```
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=..., response_mode='stream')
```

Appendix B — PR templates and example deprecation notice (copyable):
- PR title: [sdk][python] Rename streaming -> response_mode (+compat alias)
- PR body must include the checklist above and link to the ADR.
- Deprecation notice (short): "We will remove the 'streaming' alias in SDK X.Y on 2026-02-01. Please migrate to response_mode as shown in the migration guide: <link>."

Contact and questions:
- Docs and snippet issues: @Priya Nair (devx-docs)
- SDK maintainers: see OWNER file in each SDK repo.
- Migration assistance: customer-success@redwood.ai (for enterprise customers)
